newsitem.title: UK: British Labour leader calls for ban on handguns.
newsitem.headline: British Labour leader calls for ban on handguns.

text.p: British opposition leader Tony Blair, recalling the "searing, chilling, dreadful day" he visited the scene of Scotland's Dunblane school massacre, called on Tuesday for a ban on handguns.

Speaking to his Labour Party's last political conference before an election, Blair described the day he and Prime Minister John Major toured a primary school in Dunblane in March where lone gunman Thomas Hamilton murdered 16 children and a teacher before killing himself.
"It was a searing, chilling, dreadful day," Blair said. "I believe we should ban the private ownership and possession of handguns. That is our duty to the people of Dunblane."
A leading judge is due to issue his report on the massacre on October 14. The Cullen inquiry, set up by Major's government, is expected to call for tightened gun controls.
Blair criticised Conservative members of parliament opposed to a ban on handguns who, Blair said, claimed Labour's response to the Dunblane massacre had been over-emotional.
"Well, if they had been in that gym, if they had talked to those parents, sitting on the tiny chairs where once their children sat, they would have been emotional too."
In August, six Conservative members of parliament outvoted the five opposition Labour members on a parliamentary committee which considered a ban on handguns following the massacre.
Under current laws any Briton wishing to keep a handgun needs a licence from the police. Hamilton, who used four handguns in the murders, had one for years.
Lawyers for the families of the victims of Dunblane want a total ban on personal firearms but gun clubs strongly oppose the idea, saying no one can legislate for the actions of a lone maniac
